# The go command reads no go.work file and has no 'go work' command.
# GOWORK is not a go command variable.

! go work init
stderr '^go work: unknown command'

go env GOWORK
! stdout .
! go env -w GOWORK=off
stderr 'unknown go command variable GOWORK'
go env
! stdout '(set )?GOWORK='

# The go.work below names module b and replaces example.com/dep. The build
# of module a sees neither: b is not a main module, and dep keeps the
# replacement that a's own go.mod names.
cd a
go list -m
stdout '^example.com/a$'
! stdout 'example.com/b'
go list -m -f '{{.Replace.Path}}' example.com/dep
stdout '^\.\./realdep$'
go list work
stdout '^example.com/a$'
! stdout 'example.com/b'

# GOWORK in the environment names a file the go command also ignores.
env GOWORK=$WORK/gopath/src/go.work
go list -m
stdout '^example.com/a$'
! stdout 'example.com/b'

# A go.work file with no go.mod beside it does not make a module.
env GOWORK=
cd ..
! go list -m
stderr 'go.mod file not found'

-- go.work --
go 1.24

use (
	./a
	./b
)

replace example.com/dep => ./dep
-- a/go.mod --
module example.com/a

go 1.24

require example.com/dep v1.0.0

replace example.com/dep v1.0.0 => ../realdep
-- a/a.go --
package a

import _ "example.com/dep"
-- b/go.mod --
module example.com/b

go 1.24
-- b/b.go --
package b
-- dep/go.mod --
module example.com/dep

go 1.24
-- dep/dep.go --
package dep
-- realdep/go.mod --
module example.com/dep

go 1.24
-- realdep/dep.go --
package dep
